info.title: Currentfold API
info.description: The stable first-party JSON API for Currentfold clients. Integer database keys are represented as opaque decimal strings on the wire.

Subscriptions in folder and title order

post.summary: Follow a source from any site or feed URL
post.description: Resolves a pasted URL with the same autodiscovery the web uses: a YouTube channel or playlist, a feed address, or a page advertising one in <link rel="alternate">, falling back to probing the common feed paths. Two outcomes are successful and are told apart by data.status rather than by the status code. `subscribed` (201) carries the new subscription in the shape listSubscriptions returns. `candidates` (200) means the page advertised more than one feed and nothing was subscribed: present the list and POST the chosen candidate url back to this operation.

200.description: Several feeds were advertised; nothing was subscribed

201.description: The account now follows this source

get.description: Returns subscribed, non-muted articles ordered by publication date, falling back to ingest date. Pass nextCursor unchanged to continue from the prior page. Filters compose with each other and with the cursor. An unknown subscriptionId or folderId returns an empty page rather than an error.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque continuation returned by the previous response.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Which slice of the stream to return. `unread` is the absence of a read state, so an article read on another device leaves the filtered stream; `starred` and `readLater` are explicit flags.

parameters.name: unreadOnly
parameters.description: Superseded by filter=unread, and still honoured. Sending both is rejected when they disagree.

parameters.name: folderId
parameters.description: Only articles from subscriptions filed in this folder.

200.description: A keyset-paginated article page

patch.summary: Set read state for an article batch
patch.description: This operation is idempotent. Every article must belong to a feed followed by the authenticated account.

200.description: The resulting state and affected article IDs

patch.summary: Set star state for an article batch
patch.description: This operation is idempotent. Every article must belong to a feed followed by the authenticated account.

200.description: The resulting state and affected article IDs

patch.summary: Set read-later state for an article batch
patch.description: This operation is idempotent. Every article must belong to a feed followed by the authenticated account. Read-later state is independent of read state.

200.description: The resulting state and affected article IDs

post.description: Marks every unread, non-muted article in the scope read. The scope is required: there is no implicit account-wide default. With olderThan, only articles sorted strictly before that instant are marked, which is how a client marks everything below the article being read. Applying it twice is harmless; the second call reports 0.

200.description: The scope that was swept and how many articles changed

patch.summary: Store where reading stopped in an article batch
patch.description: Persists the resume position behind state.readingProgress. Batched like the other article mutations so a client can flush buffered positions in one validated request; a repeated articleId is rejected rather than resolved, since two positions for one article contradict each other. The response reports what was stored, which is not always what was sent: a fraction near either end of an article is stored as null, because resuming at the very top or the very end is worse than not resuming.

200.description: The positions that were stored

get.description: One keyset page of the account's saved web pages, ordered by save time. This is the second half of the unified Read later queue: a client merges it with GET /articles?filter=readLater by comparing savedAt against an article's publishedAt (falling back to createdAt), which is the same merge the web performs in memory. Every row carries what it needs to be drawn and read inline — no follow-up request per row.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque continuation returned by the previous response. Article cursors and saved-page cursors are not interchangeable.

200.description: A keyset-paginated saved-page page

post.summary: Save any URL to the Read later queue
post.description: Stores the link and starts fetching a readable copy in the background, so the response returns immediately — a share sheet must not wait on a publisher. The page therefore comes back with extraction.status `pending` in the ordinary case; poll listSavedPages, or retry a `failed` one. Saving is idempotent per account and canonicalized URL: saving something already in the queue returns the existing page with alreadySaved true and 200 instead of 201, and does not re-fetch it. Saves share one per-account budget with the web's bookmark and paste field.

200.description: This URL was already saved; the existing page is returned unchanged

201.description: The page was saved and its readable copy is being fetched

patch.summary: Set read state for a saved-page batch
patch.description: The saved-page half of the queue's read verb; feed articles use PATCH /articles/read-state. This operation is idempotent and validates the whole batch before writing.

200.description: The resulting state and affected saved-page IDs

patch.summary: Store where reading stopped in a saved-page batch
patch.description: The saved-page counterpart of PATCH /articles/reading-progress, with the same rules: distinct ids, whole-batch validation, and a response reporting the stored position rather than the submitted one.

200.description: The positions that were stored

delete.summary: Remove a saved page from Read later
delete.description: Remove is the read-later-only verb: a saved page is in the queue by existing, so there is no flag to clear the way a flagged feed article has one. Deleting it also deletes its readable copy and any annotations on it.

post.summary: Fetch a failed saved page's readable copy again
post.description: A deliberate retry, which is not the same as the automatic ones: it clears the attempt budget and any backoff first, so a page that gave up hours ago genuinely tries again. Unlike saving, this waits for the outcome and returns the page with its new extraction status; the status can still be `pending` when the background sweep claimed the page first.

200.description: The saved page after the retry

bearerAuth.description: A short-lived native access token or a manually issued compatibility credential. First-party clients obtain and rotate native credentials through the authentication routes.

Unauthorized.description: The bearer credential is absent, invalid, revoked, or belongs to an inactive account.

InvalidRequest.description: A query parameter or JSON body is invalid.

AccountUnavailable.description: The account or registration state does not permit this operation.

RateLimited.description: The anonymous authentication attempt budget is exhausted.

ArticleNotFound.description: At least one article is not available to this account. The error code is `article_not_found`.

ScopeNotFound.description: The named subscription or folder is not available to this account. The error code is `scope_not_found`.

SavedPageNotFound.description: At least one saved page is not available to this account. The error code is `saved_page_not_found`.

SaveLimitReached.description: The account's save budget for the current window is spent. The error code is `save_limit_reached`; Retry-After gives the seconds to wait. The budget is shared with the web's bookmark and paste field, since all three make the server fetch a URL the reader chose.

AlreadySubscribed.description: The resolved feed is one this account already follows. The error code is `already_subscribed`.

FeedNotFound.description: No feed could be resolved from that URL. The error code is `feed_not_found`; the message says what was tried or why fetching failed.

preview.description: Plain-text snippet for a list row, with the boilerplate a feed repeats in its body removed and never cut mid-word. Null when the body has nothing worth previewing.
examples: A durable readable copy of every article you follow.

readingTime.description: Estimated whole minutes to read at 225 words per minute, rounded up. Null for a stub entry under 30 words, where an estimate would be noise.

MarkAllReadRequest.description: The scope discriminates the request: `all` takes no id, `subscription` requires subscriptionId, `folder` requires folderId, and no other combination is accepted.

markedCount.description: How many articles changed from unread to read.

ReaderUrl.description: A URL a reader typed, pasted, or shared. Stored canonicalized: the scheme is added when missing, the host is lowercased, and tracking parameters and the fragment are dropped, so the same link shared twice is one entry.

title.description: The label the page gave this feed, which is how "Posts" is told from "Comments". Null when the page did not label it; show the URL instead.

ReadingProgress.description: How far through the readable body the reader got, or null for no resumable position.

positions.description: One entry per article. The articleIds must be distinct: two positions for one article contradict each other and the request is rejected rather than resolved.
One entry per saved page; the savedPageIds must be distinct.

SavedPageExtractionStatus.description: `pending` means a readable copy is still being fetched — including while a transient failure waits out its backoff, which is deliberately not shown as a failure. `ready` means content.html is the copy. `failed` is terminal until retrySavedPageExtraction is called.

url.description: The canonicalized address; also the Open original target.

title.description: The extracted title, falling back to the URL. Never empty, and available before extraction finishes.

siteName.description: What a row shows where a feed article shows its feed: the publisher name from extraction, else the URL's host without a www prefix.

savedAt.description: When the link was saved. This is the sort key of this stream and the value to merge against an article's publishedAt (or createdAt) in the unified Read later queue.

error.description: Why the copy could not be fetched. Non-null only when status is `failed`; while pending, a stored transient error is withheld because it is about to be retried.

html.description: The sanitized readable copy, safe to render directly. Null until status is `ready`.

preview.description: Row snippet, computed by the same function as an article's. Null while there is no copy to preview.

readingTime.description: Whole minutes at 225 words per minute, computed as for articles. Null while there is no copy to measure.

state.description: A saved page is in Read later by existing, so there is no readLater flag to carry, and it cannot be starred; Remove is its only exit.

alreadySaved.description: True when this URL was already in the queue. The existing page is returned unchanged and nothing is re-fetched.
